sentences: Computational differential privacy protects against efficient adversaries, whereas statistical differential privacy also protects against unbounded ones.
The 2014 textbook asks whether that relaxation can improve achievable utility when one trusted curator holds the data.
The issue is whether computational protection permits more informative outputs, beyond merely making an existing private mechanism faster.
This would show that cryptographic assumptions can change the accuracy frontier even without distributing trust across several parties.
A 2023 paper gives a conditional separation under strong cryptographic assumptions, so the textbook question is historical context rather than an unqualified assertion of present open status.
